newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Olive oil output may surge in 1996/97, prices drop.
newsitem.headline: Olive oil output may surge in 1996/97, prices drop.

text.p: Olive oil output could surge by 38 percent in 1996/1997, compared with 1995/96, and prices will fall further this year, but they should not drop below an EU intervention price, a senior industry official said.

Global production could reach 2.261 million tonnes in 1996/97, 70 percent of which comes from the European Union (EU), said Fausto Luchetti, executive director of the International Olive Oil Council (IOC).

The IOC expected production in the EU to drop slightly to 1.51 million tonnes in 1996/97 from 1.537 million in 1995/96, but production in other main centres in South America, North Africa and the Middle East was forecast to rise.
Production in Argentina was expected to rise sharply from 4,000 tonnes to 11,500 tonnes, in Tunisia by 30,000 tonnes to 250,000, and in Turkey by 10,000 to 190,000.
Consumption of olive oil was expected to exceed two million tonnes in 1996/97, compared with 1.949 million tonnes in the previous period, the IOC said.

Luchetti said during a visit to Lisbon that he expected olive oil prices to fall further this year, but that they should not drop below an EU intervention price of around 280 pesetas per kg, which will be set from July.

Asked to comment on the recent sharp drop in olive oil prices, he told a news conference: "My reaction is very sad. I think it is very bad when there are very big increases (in prices) in the sector, just as when there are big drops."
Referring to the big swings between shortages and excess production of olive oil in recent years, he added: "It is important to stabilise the olive oil market via the creation of regulatory stocks.

"This prevents prices from rising too much or dropping below a reference price. In the absence of such a stabilisation measure, producers are at the mercy of the trends of the market. We have seen that in Spain, from last year until this year, prices have dropped by practically half.
"We have just lived through three years of drought, and now we are facing a year of abundance."

Olive oil prices have been falling sharply since last September. Spanish domestic prices had fallen to 370-390 pesetas per kg in early May from just under 600 pesetas last November, the independent Oil World newsletter has said.
Luchetti was visiting Lisbon to promote an IOC conference to be held here from June 2-5. The group represents 24 countries responsible for 93 percent of the world's olive oil production.
Luchetti said there was no danger that olive oil, which costs more than other vegetable oils, would price itself out of the market because it was a high quality product.
"Buying a bottle of olive oil is an investment in good health," said Luchetti, whose group defends the interests of producers.
